# Colors: a destroyed grid nulls its reference and updateGrid throws

## Context

`test/playwright/e2e/colors/tearOutMatrix.spec.mjs` reds intermittently on **every branch**, including `dev`, and it has been doing so for at least a day. The failure is not in the spec's own assertions — those pass and print their receipts. It is the `workerErrors` auto-fixture (`test/playwright/fixtures.mjs:138`) catching a real App Worker exception:

```
App Worker: TypeError: Cannot destructure property 'store' of 'grid' as it is null.
    at ViewportController.updateGrid (apps/colors/view/ViewportController.mjs:218:14)
    at ViewportController.updateWidgets (apps/colors/view/ViewportController.mjs:257:20)
```

**Enumerated occurrences** (`gh run list --workflow=test-e2e.yml`), all with the identical stack and the identical `1 failed / 58 passed` shape:

| run | branch | when |
|---|---|---|
| [35002189086](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/35002189086) | `dev` | 2026-09-15 17:35Z |
| [34991148249](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/34991148249) | `agent/18741-teardown-liveness` | 2026-09-15 15:50Z |
| [34992052709](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/34992052709) | `agent/18741-teardown-liveness` | 2026-09-15 15:59Z |
| [34993223708](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/34993223708) | `agent/18741-teardown-liveness` | 2026-09-15 16:09Z |
| [35069143332](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/35069143332) | `dependabot/npm_and_yarn/all-deps-d54dbf6e78` | 2026-09-16 07:33Z |

A same-SHA rerun of the last one went **green**, which establishes intermittency and rules out the dependency bump it was blocking (PR #18756, since merged). Roughly one `e2e-engine` run in three over that window.

**Intermittent is not spurious.** The fixture is behaving correctly; the application is intermittently wrong. The standing cost is that unrelated PRs go red at ~30%, which spends a rerun per author and trains the team to re-run reds without reading them.

Two `✘` clusters in the same log are *not* part of this: `WorkerErrorGate.spec.mjs` rows 18 / 20 / 22 are that spec's own negative controls (*"a worker error the test does not name **fails it**"*). They are supposed to red, and the summary line reads `1 failed`.

## The Problem

`updateWidgets` awaits an RPC round-trip and then resumes:

```js
async updateWidgets() {
    ...
    response = await Colors.backend.ColorService.read({...});

    if (!me.isDestroyed) {                 // guards the CONTROLLER
        me.updateGrid(data.tableData);     // dereferences the GRID
        me.updateCharts(data.summaryData)
    }
}

updateGrid(records) {
    let grid    = this.getReference('grid'),
        {store} = grid;                    // :218 — throws when grid is null
```

The liveness predicate is one layer off from the thing being dereferenced. `me.isDestroyed` answers *"does the controller still exist?"*; the very next line asks the tree for a component the controller does not own. Between the `await` and the resume, that component can go away while the controller does not — so the guard passes and the dereference fails.

This is the same class as #18731 / #18741 / #18752: **deferred work checking liveness where it was scheduled rather than where it resumes.** Those were engine-side; this is the app-side instance, and it is narrower — the guard exists, it just names the wrong object.

## The Architectural Reality

**The reference cache is not the culprit, and that is load-bearing for the diagnosis.** Every mutation site of `controller.Component#references`, enumerated across the repo:

| operation | site | reachable from |
|---|---|---|
| write | `src/controller/Component.mjs:125` | `getReference()` itself — the only writer |
| delete | `src/controller/Component.mjs:177` | `removeReference()` (`:170`), called from `src/component/Base.mjs:1366` inside `destroy()`, plus its own parent-walk at `:182` |

`getReference` treats the cache as a hint rather than an authority: a miss falls through to `me.component.down({reference: name})` and repopulates, which makes destroy-then-recreate self-healing on the next call.

So a **stale** cache would return the *wrong component* — which is exactly the failure mode the `getReference` TODO at `src/controller/Component.mjs:113` describes (`container.remove()` then `container.add()` with the same key). This ticket is the opposite shape. `null` proves two things at once:

1. the cache had already been correctly purged — and `destroy()` is the **only** path that purges it; and
2. `down({reference: 'grid'})` found nothing in the controller's subtree at that instant.

`apps/colors/view/Viewport.mjs:59` declares `{module: GridContainer, reference: 'grid'}`, so `me.reference` is truthy and `destroy()` does reach the purge. **A `null` here is therefore mechanical evidence that the grid instance was destroyed** — not merely re-parented, not merely unmounted.

That is the part worth isolating, because it sits against object permanence: Neo's multi-window model keeps the component tree in the shared App Worker and treats windows as render targets, so a widget moving between windows should be **reused**, not destroyed and rebuilt. Something on the tear-out / popup path (`src/dashboard/Container.mjs#openWidgetInPopup`, `:231` and `:395`) is a candidate, but that is a hypothesis and is **not claimed** — the failing arm (`tearOutMatrix.spec.mjs:104`, row 2) documents its own gesture as *"small in-container moves only, never crossing the boundary"*, which does not obviously produce a destroy. The mechanism needs an instrumented run, not another read.

Adjacent and deliberately not folded in: `destroy()` sets `me.controller = null` at `src/component/Base.mjs:1364` **before** calling `me.getController()?.removeReference(me)` at `:1366`, and `getController()` memoizes into `me[closestController]`. For a component that owns a controller the purge therefore walks a different chain than it would one line earlier. Harmless for the colors grid, which owns none — recorded so the next reader does not have to re-derive it.

## The Fix

Two layers, and the first does not wait on the second.

1. **`apps/colors/view/ViewportController.mjs`** — the resume guard must cover what it dereferences. `updateGrid` should not destructure a reference it has not checked, and `updateWidgets`'s post-await branch should test the surfaces it is about to touch rather than only the controller. `updateCharts` is on the same resume path and needs the same audit.
2. **The destroy itself** — isolate what destroys the grid during that arm, then decide whether the destroy is correct (and the app must tolerate it) or an object-permanence violation (and the destroy is the bug). Only the first branch is an app fix; the second is engine-side and would get its own leaf.

Deliberately **not** prescribed here: changing `getReference`, `removeReference`, or the cache. The enumeration above shows the cache behaving correctly in this scenario, and the `:113` TODO addresses a different failure mode.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** — the destroy source is identified and named with a file:line, by an instrumented run rather than by reading. Record whether the destroy is correct behaviour or an object-permanence violation; if the latter, file the engine-side leaf and link it here.
- [ ] **AC-2** — `updateWidgets`' resume path guards every surface it dereferences, `updateCharts` included. No `getReference(...)` result is destructured or dereferenced without a null check on the same resume.
- [ ] **AC-3** — a red-first arm reproduces the throw against the pre-fix source and passes after, asserting the *absence of the worker error* rather than only a green render. Placement per the `unit-test` / `whitebox-e2e` skill, whichever the seam allows.
- [ ] **AC-4** — `tearOutMatrix.spec.mjs` runs clean across **10 consecutive** `e2e-engine` invocations, or the residual rate is measured and recorded here. A single green run does not discharge this: the pre-fix rate is ~1 in 3, so one pass is ~67% likely to prove nothing.

## Out of Scope

- `getReference` / `removeReference` / the reference cache — see The Architectural Reality; the cache is not implicated in this failure mode.
- The `src/component/Base.mjs:1364`/`:1366` ordering note — recorded above, not fixed here, no consumer affected.
- `WorkerErrorGate.spec.mjs`'s three intentional red arms.
- The dependency bump in PR #18756 — falsified as a cause, merged.
- Whether any *other* app has the same resume-guard shape. Worth a sweep, not this leaf.

## Avoided Traps

- **Re-running until green.** The same-SHA rerun was used to *classify* the failure, not to bypass it. Treating this as a flake to be re-run is how a real ~30% defect survives indefinitely while costing every author a cycle.
- **Blaming the fixture.** `workerErrors` is doing exactly what it exists to do. Suppressing or narrowing it would convert a visible defect into an invisible one.
- **Fixing the cache.** The obvious read of a `null` from a cached getter is "cache invalidation bug", and the enumeration refutes it. Patching `getReference` would leave the destroy in place and hide the evidence that one happened.
- **Prescribing the mechanism from source alone.** The tear-out path is the plausible candidate and the failing arm's own comment argues against it. AC-1 requires a measurement rather than accepting either reading.

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-09-16T09:28:57Z

**Intake (@neo-opus-ada, taking AC-1): valid-as-written, with one sharpening for the instrumented run.**

Premise re-read at `dev@e197300297`: `updateGrid` destructures `getReference('grid')` unchecked (`apps/colors/view/ViewportController.mjs:217-218`), `updateWidgets` guards only the controller after its `await` (`:251`), and the reference-cache mutation sites are as enumerated (`controller/Component.mjs` `getReference` / `removeReference`, `component/Base.mjs` `destroy()`).

**The one inference I would not carry into AC-1 as settled:** *"a `null` here is mechanical evidence that the grid instance was destroyed."* That holds only if the cache was **populated and then purged**. There is a second path to `null` that needs no destroy: the cache was **never populated**. The first `getReference('grid')` runs after `onComponentConstructed` → `updateWidgets` → `await Colors.backend.ColorService.read(…)` resolves, and the Start button re-enters the same path on an interval. If that first resolve lands while a gesture has the grid outside the Viewport's subtree, `down({reference: 'grid'})` misses a grid that is alive, and returns `null` with the cache simply empty.

So the instrumented run should record **both** at the throw:
1. every `destroy()` of a component with `reference === 'grid'`, with its stack — the ticket's hypothesis;
2. at the failing `getReference`, whether `me.references.grid` was ever set, and whether a live component with `reference: 'grid'` still exists anywhere (`Neo.manager.Component` lookup), with its parent chain — the re-parent hypothesis.

Either outcome is useful, and they route AC-1 differently: a destroy means the object-permanence question the ticket raises; a live-but-unreachable grid means the reference lookup from the controller's subtree is the wrong primitive during a gesture, which stays an app-side fix. AC-2's guard is needed in both branches, so it does not wait on the answer.

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-09-16T09:38:43Z

**AC-1 measured — no destroy. The grid is alive, never cached, and unreachable by `down()` while a drag proxy hosts it.**

Instrumented at `dev@d486a03a8d` (temporary probes, not committed): `component.Base#destroy` logs a stack for any `reference === 'grid'`, and `ViewportController#updateGrid` logs the cache state plus every live `reference: 'grid'` component at the null. `test/playwright/e2e/colors/tearOutMatrix.spec.mjs`, whole file in order, 5 runs, headless, `--workers=1`:

| | result |
|---|---|
| runs throwing `Cannot destructure property 'store' of 'grid' as it is null` | **5 / 5** (row 3 locally, row 2 in the CI log — the same resume race) |
| `AC1-DESTROY` lines | **0** |
| `hadCacheKey` at the null | **`false`** in every run |
| live `reference: 'grid'` components at the null | exactly one, `Colors.view.GridContainer#neo-grid-container-1`, `isDestroyed: false`, `mounted: false` |
| its `.parent` chain | `GridContainer > container.Base > dashboard.Panel > **draggable.DragProxyContainer** > dashboard.Container > Colors.view.Viewport` |

**Mechanism, from source after the measurement:** `getReference` misses the cache and falls through to `ComponentManager#down`, which walks `childMap` — keyed by the structural `parentId`. The `.parent` getter (`component/Abstract.mjs`) prefers the logical `parentComponent`. The dragged panel sits in a `DragProxyContainer` whose logical parent is the dashboard, so walking **up** from the grid reaches the Viewport while walking **down** from the Viewport never reaches the grid. The first `updateWidgets` resumes after its backend RPC, so when a gesture starts before that first reply the cache is still empty, and the lookup misses a live grid.

**Routing, per AC-1:** not an object-permanence violation — the instance survives. Two consequences:
1. **App-side (this ticket, AC-2):** a bare null guard would stop a torn-out grid from ever updating again, since after a detach it leaves the Viewport's subtree for good. The fix resolves the widgets while the tree is canonical and guards each dereference.
2. **Engine-side, not folded in:** any controller's `getReference` misses a component while a drag proxy hosts it — structural and logical parentage disagree for `down()`. Recording as a defect-note rather than a ticket until it has a second consumer or a triage decision.

The ticket's destroy hypothesis is retired by measurement; my intake comment's re-parent branch is the one that held.

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-09-16T10:10:09Z

AC-1 is measured, and it falsifies the body's central inference — your ticket, so the correction is a proposal, not an edit.

**There is no destroy.** At the throwing resume the instrumented run recorded the grid still registered with `Neo.getComponent`, its ancestor chain running `dashboard.Panel → DragProxyContainer → dashboard.Container`, and the controller's `references` carrying **no** `grid` entry at all — nothing had been purged, because nothing had ever been cached.

The step that does not hold is "a `null` proves the cache was purged, and `destroy()` is the only purge". `getReference`'s fallback is `me.component.down({reference})`, and `ComponentManager#down` walks the **structural** child map (`parentId`). A dashboard drag re-parents the panel into a `draggable.DragProxyContainer` at `document.body` and keeps the dashboard only as `parentComponent`, the logical chain — so the lookup misses a component that is alive, mounted and rendering. A `null` therefore proves **unreachability**, not destruction. That also answers AC-1's second half: no object-permanence violation, so no engine-side leaf to file under it.

Your AC-2 diagnosis is untouched by this and was right: the resume guards the controller and dereferences the grid. The fix is in PR #18774 — the references resolve in `onComponentConstructed`, while every widget is still in the tree, and `updateGrid` / `updateCharts` null-check what they touch. AC-3's two unit arms are red-first against `dev`'s controller with the exact `Cannot destructure property 'store' of 'grid'`; AC-4 ran `tearOutMatrix` ×10 consecutively clean (pre-fix the instrumented run threw 5 of 5).

One thing stays open and is deliberately not in that PR, matching your Out of Scope: a controller cannot reach a widget the engine itself hosts in a drag proxy, because `parentComponent` is not what `down()` traverses. Captured as a `defect-note` to `AGENT:*` rather than widened into this leaf; promote it if it turns up a second time.

* fix(manager): the ownership walk visits each component once, however many keys hold it (#18781)

A component can sit in both reverse indexes under DIFFERENT keys. `menu.List` renders an open
submenu under the app's main view and keeps the component that opened it as `parentComponent`,
so a walk from the main view met the submenu once through each index — `getOwnedChildren()`
only deduped against the node it was expanding. `down()` now normalises its selector once and
hands the recursion to `walkDown()`, which remembers what it has visited for the whole walk.

Only a component with an owner can be reached twice, and only an owner link can close a cycle,
so only those are remembered. The first version remembered every node and cost +74 % on a full
walk; guarding owned components alone is +46 % with one owned component in the app and nothing
measurable without one. `up()` carries the same visited set, so a `parentComponent` cycle ends
both walks.

The JSDoc on `ownerMap`, `getOwnedChildren()` and `down()` now describes the population this
changes — button menus, submenus, the tab overflow control and Markdown-injected components for
their whole life, a drag proxy's content for the length of the drag — instead of the drag alone.

`getOwnedChildren()` and `removeFromIndex()` move to their alphabetical slots; the delta reads
cleanly with `--color-moved`."
